claims.statement: Documentation precedence in this repository is code first: AGENTS.md explicitly tells readers that docs/design.md is a product spec that is partly aspirational and that the code should be trusted for what is implemented, and no other document overrides source.

AGENTS.md documents images as served under /data/images with API paths like data/images/... while server/src/main.rs mounts image_dir at /images and services::image::save_image stores subdirectory-relative paths such as items/{uuid}.ext.

The image extension allow-list includes avif in addition to jpg/jpeg/png/webp, and an avif upload short-circuits thumbnail generation so its thumb_path equals its file_path; AGENTS.md still lists only the four older formats.

AGENTS.md's claim that web/src/components/ui is empty scaffolding is wrong: the directory contains eight working components (ConfirmDialog, DocumentList, ImageUpload, Lightbox, MarkdownText, PdfPreview, Select, Skeleton), clsx/tailwind-merge/lucide-react are imported by them, and only class-variance-authority and react-dropzone are genuinely unused dependencies.

AGENTS.md's assertion that the repo has no lint/format config and no CI is stale: rustfmt.toml, web/.prettierrc and web/.prettierignore exist, the justfile defines fmt/lint/check recipes, and .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml is a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow; only a pre-commit hook and code-test CI are absent.

Default runtime paths are XDG-based — $XDG_DATA_HOME/wheremystuff or ~/.local/share/wheremystuff holding wheremystuff.db, images/ and docs/ — and fall back to relative data/ only when neither XDG_DATA_HOME nor HOME is set, contradicting AGENTS.md's data/wheremystuff.db and data/images defaults.

The SPA is embedded into the binary at compile time via rust_embed over ../web/dist, so the binary no longer serves web/dist from the filesystem at runtime; the surviving working-directory dependency is the relative lookup of config.toml (plus the relative data/ fallback), making AGENTS.md's repo-root requirement and the Containerfile comment stale.
The FTS table indexes items.location_note in addition to the fields AGENTS.md lists; migration 0003 recreates items_fts with that column and sync_item populates it from the items row.

Only item create and item update call search_index::sync_item, so renames of tags, containers, and categories do not refresh affected items and search results can stay stale until the startup sync_all rebuild — the resync gap AGENTS.md warns about is still real.

docs/design.md's frontend project tree names files that do not exist (App.tsx, SearchBar/ContainerTree/ItemCard/ItemForm/ImageGallery/TagInput/CategorySelect components, tailwind.config.ts) and omits routes/items/$id/edit.tsx; the real shared components live in web/src/components/ui/.

docs/design.md documents trigger-based FTS synchronization while the implementation syncs explicitly from backend code: there are no triggers in any migration and index maintenance goes through services::search_index::sync_item/sync_all.

docs/design.md's ER model is missing items.location_note and the entire item_documents table added by migrations 0002 and 0003, and it describes source_type as only purchased or handmade while the UI exposes five values.

README.md contradicts itself on runtime data location — the install section says a data/ directory is created in the current working directory while the configuration section documents $XDG_DATA_HOME/wheremystuff — and server/src/config.rs implements the XDG variant; README.en.md carries both statements too.

README dev and nginx guidance still routes media under /data/images, but the binary mounts /images and web/vite.config.ts only proxies /api and the obsolete /data/images prefix, so media requests to /images are not proxied during Vite development.

No automated tests exist: server/tests/ is absent, no module contains #[cfg(test)], and `just test` runs `cargo test -p server` over zero tests, so README's Tests & Linting section and AGENTS.md's test command describe a suite that does not exist.

The OpenWiki GitHub workflow runs daily at 08:00 UTC and on workflow_dispatch, runs `openwiki code --update --print` with continue-on-error, deletes openwiki/.run.json, then opens or updates a pull request on branch openwiki/update staging openwiki, AGENTS.md, the workflow file, and CLAUDE.md when present, re-raising failure at the end so partial pages still land in the PR.

Because AGENTS.md is in the workflow's add-paths, OpenWiki owns the content between OPENWIKI:START and OPENWIKI:END there; edits inside that block are regenerated, and AGENTS.md instructs readers not to hand-edit generated OpenWiki pages but to change source code or docs instead.

source_type is a five-value vocabulary (purchased, handmade, gift, salvage, other) rendered with Chinese labels by sourceTypeLabel, the DB default is handmade, and the option lists are duplicated in routes/items/new.tsx and routes/items/$id/edit.tsx, so adding a value requires editing all three places.
An item with no container path is displayed as 未归位 by containerPathText, a render-time fallback rather than a stored value, which the forms also use as the empty-select placeholder.

Item descriptions are rendered as Markdown through MarkdownText, which uses react-markdown with img elements disallowed and unwrapped, while all UI copy is Chinese; both conventions are absent from the prose docs.

The container deployment relies on a data volume at /app/data mounted from ./data, but the binary's default data paths resolve to the XDG location, so persistence through that volume is only guaranteed if the container has neither HOME nor XDG_DATA_HOME set; the systemd unit documents the XDG behavior while the Containerfile comment still claims cwd-relative web/dist and data.

Generated artifacts and their regeneration paths are distinct: web/src/routeTree.gen.ts comes from the TanStack router plugin and is committed but prettier-ignored, web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo comes from tsc -b and is gitignored, Cargo.lock and web/pnpm-lock.yaml are committed cargo/pnpm outputs with the container build requiring a frozen lockfile, and web/dist plus target are build outputs that are never edited.
